sections.html:
Buena Vista County sits in northwest Iowa with Storm Lake as seat and largest city. The 2020 count was 20,823 people, and Storm Lake alone had 11,269 of them. Alta follows with 2,087, then a string of small towns from Newell (906) down to Truesdale (69).

Lakeside, on the east shore of Storm Lake, is its own small city, separate from Storm Lake itself. If your address is by the water, check the parcel record to see which city it falls in, since that affects which levies appear on the bill.

One office takes the money and the other sets the value, and you reach both at 215 E. 5th Street in Storm Lake. Weekday hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Buena Vista County property tax offices
OfficePhoneMailing address
Treasurer712-749-2533P.O. Drawer 149, Storm Lake, IA 50588
Assessor712-749-2543P.O. Box 148, Storm Lake, IA 50588

Look for the property tax window on the courthouse's ground level. Payment works through iowatreasurers.org, the mail, a secure box on the building's east side, or a visit in person.

Your bill splits into two halves. Pay the first by September 30. The second can be paid March 1 through March 31. Miss either and a penalty of 1.5 percent per month builds, beginning October 1 for the fall half. A postmark on or before the deadline is accepted, and an online payment counts until 11:59 p.m. that evening. Saturday and Sunday deadlines slide to Monday.

Send the stubs from your statement with a check so it posts to the correct parcel.

  • August: statements are mailed.
  • September 30: first half deadline.
  • March 31: second half deadline.
  • June: annual tax sale of delinquent parcels.

Real property gets a fresh valuation every other year, the odd-numbered ones, using a January 1 snapshot. Informal review runs April 2 to April 25, and a formal protest to the Board of Review runs April 2 to April 30. In odd years, appeals of an equalization order can be filed October 9 to 31.

Hearings start May 1 and continue until the board adjourns. Members include a farmer, a real estate agent and a person who knows construction. Disagree with the ruling and your options are the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court. A disaster proclamation can stretch these windows to May 25 and June 5.

Starting with assessment year 2026, the homestead credit became a homestead exemption. It equals 10 percent of the home's taxable value, with a minimum of $5,500 and a maximum of $20,000, and the claim is due by July 1. Those with military service may also qualify for a $4,000 military exemption. The assessor handles both, so call 712-749-2543 if you are unsure what is on your parcel.

Whoever buys the house files their own claim after closing, ideally before July 1 so it starts on the next bill.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the June tax sale
sections.html:
Parcels with unpaid tax go to a yearly auction at the courthouse each June, and all bids are placed online. Redemption cannot be handled through the website. Call 712-749-2533 or visit the treasurer.

To redeem, an owner pays the delinquent tax plus 2 percent for every month since the sale. The county publishes a delinquent tax list every year plus a notice for tax sale purchasers. Scan the list before advertising a house to learn whether the parcel is already queued for June. A payoff number for a chosen closing date is available from the treasurer.

The seller pays Iowa's transfer tax: 80 cents for every $500 of value past the first $500. Collection happens at the recorder's desk, where a declaration of value accompanies the deed. A few transfers escape it under Iowa Code section 428A.2, including spouse-to-spouse or parent-to-child gifts and estate distributions to heirs that involve no payment.

Owners in Storm Lake, Alta or a smaller town whose taxes or repairs have piled up can look at a cash sale as-is, which closes without a listing or showings. The tax payoff and recording steps still apply.

Call the treasurer first. Request a payoff covering both halves plus any penalty through the date you expect to close, then check the delinquent list for your parcel number. Next, contact the assessor about the homestead exemption and any military exemption, because a buyer will want to know what stays and what must be refiled. Then gather the deed so the declaration of value can go in at recording. Once these pieces are collected, the title company can set the closing, deduct the tax from your proceeds, and send the deed to the recorder. Pay attention to your own calendar too: a sale that closes in late spring or summer may fall before the first July 1 claim deadline, which gives the new owner time to file for the exemption.

sections.h2: Walking through a sale with taxes owed
sections.html:
Picture a Storm Lake owner who fell behind on the fall half. Interest has been building since October 1, and if the parcel reaches the June auction it lands on the delinquent list. At that stage the number to learn is the redemption amount, which is the tax sold plus the monthly charge. Ask the treasurer for it in writing with a date the figure stays good, hand it to the title company, and let the closing pay it from your proceeds. Nothing about this blocks a sale. It only adds a line to the settlement statement.

If the parcel has not been sold, the process is shorter: confirm the balance, pay it at closing, and keep the receipt.

sections.h2: Questions to put to the assessor
sections.html: Call 712-749-2543 and ask which exemptions are on file. Ask whether your parcel is in a reassessment year, because values are reset every two years and a buyer may ask what is coming. Ask when informal review opens, since a short talk in April may settle a disagreement before it needs a formal protest. If the property sits near the lake, ask which city levies apply, and make sure the address on the bill matches the parcel record.

Two postings are worth a look before you list. The delinquent tax list shows which parcels are headed to auction, and the notice to tax sale purchasers describes how bidding works for the year. Neither is an invitation to wait. A parcel that has not been sold can still be cleared with the treasurer at any time, and the earlier you do it the less interest the balance collects, so a quick call is worth making.

faqs.q: When are Buena Vista County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Fall half by September 30, spring half by March 31. After that, 1.5 percent per month is added.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Buena Vista County property tax?
faqs.a: Visit 215 E. 5th Street in Storm Lake, or use iowatreasurers.org, the mail, or the east-side drop box.

faqs.q: How often does Buena Vista County reassess property?
faqs.a: Every second year, the odd ones, with January 1 as the valuation date.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Buena Vista County assessment?
faqs.a: Formal protests go to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30. An informal review with the assessor is open April 2 to April 25.

faqs.q: Can I redeem a property after the tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, within the time Iowa law allows. Call the treasurer at 712-749-2533 or visit in person, because redemption cannot be paid through the website.
